name: Salvation by grace through faith
about: Saved by grace through faith in Christ, without works.

teachings.title: Abel's blood sacrifice and Cain's works
teachings.summary: Abel was accepted by faith in the blood sacrifice while Cain was rejected for offering his own works, and the shedding of innocent blood cries out from the earth and brings judgment on a land.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:4**
*By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.*

Now fallen, cast out from Eden, Adam and Eve, the mother of man are fruitful and multiply.

And her first born, a man from God is Cain, a tiller of the earth. Working the fields.

We know from Genesis 3 the burden God placed on fallen man.

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

Cain, under this burden grew herbs and vegetables, fruit of the land. With sweat of his brow. *Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the* Lord*.*

And God respected not his sacrifice.

And Abel, a keeper of sheep, *he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the* Lord *had respect unto Abel and to his offering.*

The firstling lamb. The sacrifice of blood for attornment. The Bible says Abel *by faith* brought the sacrifice that was acceptable unto the Lord.

But Cain brought his works and was rejected.

But God, long suffering and who the Bible says would not that any man perish, gives His word to Cain, to repent towards the faith, in the blood of the lamb for remission of sin, as He had given Adam and Eve, that Abel gained God's pleasure by.

*And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.*

Unable to get past his own pride and accept God's promise, His word, Cain allowed his wrath in, and in covetousness slew innocent Abel, and the very earth cries out to the Lord that his blood had been spilled.

This is a Biblical doctrine that's often overlooked. The spilling of innocent blood actually causes the earth itself to cry out to God. We see several times throughout scripture God warns man against it;

*That innocent blood be not shed in thy land, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.*
**Deuteronomy 19:10**

*For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now*.
**Romans 8:22**

*The blood of their sons and their daughters,*
*Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan;*
*And the land was polluted with the blood.*
**Psalm 106:38**

One of the things that curses a land and brings judgement on a people is innocent blood shed. It pollutes the land, and the earth travails and groans, crying out to the Lord.

And so undone, Cain is cursed.

When we reject God's word, His gift of salvation in the blood of Christ, the lamb slain at the foundation of the world,  when we count on our works and want credit from God for our own righteousness, we invite sin into our heart, and when we reject God's word finally, are rejected of Him. Marked as Cain.

teachings.title: Then began men to call upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Since the generation of Enos all men have been saved the same way, by faith in the Lord, calling upon His name, as Romans 10:13 and Joel 2:32 declare.
teachings.text:
*And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.*

*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*
**Romans 10:13**

*And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.*
**Acts 2:21**

*And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.*
**Joel 2:32**

The first generation of man had the sure word of God directly to them, of the faith in the Lord to deliver them. The blood sacrifice as atonement. The promise of eternal life in the Lord, who is our salvation.

This is the faith which all man has been saved by, in Christ Jesus, since the world began.

And as Enos' generation came to be, and the faith given the father's by God's word handed down, men began to call upon the name of the Lord for salvation.

Jesus the same yesterday, today and forever.

*But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*
**John 1:12**

teachings.title: Abraham believed God and was counted righteous
teachings.summary: Like Abraham, whose belief in God's promise was imputed to him for righteousness, salvation has always been by hearing and believing God's word, by faith alone and not by works.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 11:8**
*By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.*

**James 2:23**
 *And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.*

**2 Chronicles 20:7**
*Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?*

Abraham believed. This is the verb form of faith, the noun, the thing Abraham had. He believed having faith in God's word. His promise. And that faith was imputed upon him for righteousness and he was called *the friend of God.*

If we believe, an action, if we have faith, the evidence of things unseen, a thing to possess, in the word of God, His promises, His testimony, we have His righteousness imputed on us. Projected upon us. Not our own righteousness. Not our works. But our faith, which comes from believing, which comes from the word of God.

O, to be called the friend of God for our faith!

Salvation has always been by hearing the word of God, believing it, which gives us faith to call upon the name of the Lord, for which God grants us His grace.

 Salvation is by faith alone. Yesterday, today and forever, amen.

teachings.title: The sabbath, a picture of rest in Christ
teachings.summary: The sabbath pictures resting in Christ's finished work, so salvation is by faith alone, and keeping the seventh-day sabbath to be saved, as Seventh-day Adventists do, is judaized bondage while Christians gather on the Lord's day.
teachings.text:
**Mark 2:28**
*Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.*

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

Chapter 31 provides an additional teaching on the sabbath, God instructs Moses to tell the people they are not to work on the last day of the week, least they be cut off and put to death. That the sabbath is a day of rest to memorialize His perpetual covenant, that it is by faith in the Lord that sanctifies us.

It is a fitting picture of Christ, in whom we are called to rest on His perfect work for salvation. That salvation is by faith alone, not of works. And if you reach the end and are trusting in your works rather than the sabbath God provided, you're perishing. You will be cast out and put to death, which is Hell.

People struggling with the idea that our works do not save us don't understand how the Sabbath is a memorial for the covenant of Christ. That we are free of the yoke of the law in regards to righteousness, because by the blood of Christ God will not impute sin to those that are saved when we are called to the Kingdom. They miss the point of the 3 sabbaths in a row between Passover and Easter Sunday, the first day of the week. That no works of the law shall save us. Jesus did it all.

7th Day Adventists and others under the yoke of the law keep the old testament sabbath, the last day of the week, in order to be saved. It is judaized nonsense.

Christians celebrate and gather on the first day of the week, the Lord's day, in remembrance of His resurrection and the establishment of the new testament. As a memorial throughout our generations that we may know He is the Lord that sanctifies us.

**Galatians 5:1**
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.*

teachings.title: Righteousness by faith, not circumcision
teachings.summary: Abraham was counted righteous by faith before circumcision, so no rite, baptism, or work is required for salvation, and the inheritance is by faith in Christ, not by fleshly descent as Zionism and dispensationalism claim.
teachings.text:
So this is the promise made by God that if we believe on the Son, we are saved by His grace. Our sins forgiven. No sin even being imputed upon us. Whether we work or not, because work is debt not grace.

Paul continues using Abraham's example;

*Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.*

Abraham did not receive the ordinance of circumcision until decades after his believing God's promise, and being saved by that faith. He was blessed with the accounting of righteousness when he did not know circumcision. So this promise, predating this rite of the Jews, means it does not only apply to the circumcised, but also to the uncircumcised. And so the promise of grace doesn't require circumcision, but faith alone.

This point is both specific to the issue of circumcision being introduced by the Judaizers in Paul's day, but also generally speaking, that there is no rite or ordinance that is required for salvation. Not baptism. Not any ritual or keeping of tradition. No works of the law.

*And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also*.

Abraham as the father of all who believe, the circumcision of the spirit, the generation of believers are partakers of the promise, that the righteousness of God is imputed upon us in faith.

*For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression.*

The promise of God that Abraham believed was that through his faith, he would be made father to many nations, and inherit the kingdom of God. This promise was made possible in Christ.

**Galatians 3:16**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

Unbelieving Jews felt they were owed the kingdom by God for being Abraham's seed under the law. That the inheritance was by blood, and the promise made to them after the flesh, and not in the spirit.

This is the basis for Zionism and the false doctrine of dispensationalism.

But the Bible teaches the exact opposite. There is no difference between Jew and Gentile. All are under sin. It is by faith only that we are made heirs. That the seed of the promise is Christ manifest in the flesh.

**Matthew 3:9**
*And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.*

It is not an inheritance by the law but by faith. Like Esua and Jacob, the inheritance went to the younger. It was taken from the elder, who with tears sought repentance from God, but none was found.

**Luke 13:25-30**
*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God. And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.*

teachings.title: Easy-believism and the strait gate
teachings.summary: Salvation by believing on Christ alone, mocked as easy-believism, is the strait gate few find, because pride, works and the false hope of repent-of-your-sins preachers keep men from simply trusting that Jesus paid it all.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**Acts 16:30-31**
*And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

This is the Gospel of faith, taught throughout the Bible. But it is derisively called "easy-believism" by those seeking to bring another gospel of works and self-righteousness.

If believing the Gospel for salvation were "easy," then why do so many people struggle with trusting in Christ Jesus alone for their salvation? Why does every false religion reject this simple faith for works and penance?

**Matthew 7:13-14**
*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Believing on Christ alone for salvation is the narrow way. The strait gate. And there really are few who find it.

Pride and vanity and inability to trust the word of God keeps people from letting go and trusting by faith. They want reassurance that it "worked" before they can let go. They are carrying so much of a burden, and yoked by the law, that they cannot fit through that strait gate. Like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle. And so they seek a wider path to their own destruction.

Or they want to force their way through by exhibiting signs of deserving it through their own acts of righteousness, which the Bible calls filthy rags. Greasing the entrance by their own good intentions, so that they can accept that they "deserve" to enter. Not realizing none deserve it, but we are given entrance through Christ.

They want to know without trust, so that they may believe, and so they never can come to the knowledge of the truth. Because *faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*. And without visible evidence, they doubt, and are given false hope from the "Repent-of-your-sins" types who claim that they may know they are saved if they do certain acts, and behave a certain way. But that false hope gives way when any weight is put upon it, because their standards are impossible to achieve in the flesh. It is impossible to pass through that gate carrying our own works, which are wood, hay and stubble, fit to be burned.

We don't begin to be sanctified until we are in the kingdom already. Until we have passed through that gate. Without faith, it is impossible to please God.

So don't be fooled. Salvation is easy, from a works standpoint because it doesn't require any effort from us to believe that Jesus paid it all. But it is hard from a human standpoint, letting go of all the burdens that keep us from passing through.

teachings.title: Rahab and the scarlet thread
teachings.summary: Rahab the harlot was saved by her faith in God and placed in the line of Christ, her scarlet thread a picture of His blood, showing God can redeem anyone who holds the faith.
teachings.text:
And so we are here in **Joshua** chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land.

His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in **Numbers 13**, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good.

Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear.

Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan.

She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved.

Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible.

And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew;

**Matthew 1:5-6**
*And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias*

The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread.

And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in **Hebrews 11**, in the company of great Old Testament believers;

**Hebrews 11:31**
*By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace*.

She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart;

**James 2:25**
*Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?*

Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith.

teachings.title: Precept upon precept on the cornerstone
teachings.summary: Jesus is the rejected stone made the head of the corner, the only foundation, and believers grow line upon line building works on Him that will be tried at judgment.
teachings.text:
Isaiah continues to speak the word of God, now against Israel and Judah. The princes who are drunk with wine and cannot rule justly. The priests and prophets, who err in vision and stumble in judgment. Vision often being the understanding and knowledge of the word of God, they preach vain things. Their tables full of vomit. Literally and spiritually.

*Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts*.

**Hebrews 5:13-14**
*For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.*

We learn the word, precept upon precept. Built like a wall, upon the cornerstone, level and plumb. Square and true. Line upon line. Here a little, there a little.

**Psalm 119:104**
*Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.*

Jesus is that cornerstone laid for us. The rock of our salvation upon which we stand. Like the wise man who built his home upon it.

**Psalm 118:22**
*The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.*

**Matthew 21:42**
*Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?*

**Acts 4:11**
*This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.*

**1 Peter 2:7-8**
*Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.*

There is no other foundation upon which man can built that doesn't come to naught, but Jesus. And we build up on that rock, precept by precept. Here a little, there a little. Until we are raised to judgment, and eternal life.

**Matthew 7:24**
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock*

**1 Corinthians 3:11-15**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

Amen

teachings.title: A new song of His great salvation
teachings.summary: Psalm 40 rejoices in God's deliverance from the miry pit of sin onto the rock Christ, showing that God never required sacrifices to save but only faith in His promises, which comes by hearing His word and calling on His name.
teachings.text:
After the somber and broken-hearted appeal of **Psalm 39**, **Psalm 40** gives us the rejoicing of those that trust in the Lord, and declares His power to all.

How wonderful is our patient waiting on the Lord, having called out His name for deliverance, to be rewarded by seeing Him turn towards us to save us in love!

He frees us from the miry pit of sin, He delivers us out of tribulation and temptations. He brings us from the shifting sands of doubt and fear, and sets us upon a rock. Our rock, Christ Jesus. The solid ground where He establishes our goings, and directs our paths. Praise Jesus for His great salvation!

We who are saved have a new song in our heart, the gospel which we preach, the good news of eternal life and forgiveness in Christ, *even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD*.

*Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies.*

Is there any better news than this? Repenting from lies to trust in the Lord, and the blessings that we are given by His grace in exchange. Eternal life, His perfect word, His judgments. The Spirit of truth. The rejection of the proud. The deliverance from the evil of others. Made sons of God and joint-heirs with Jesus. Many are the wonderful works that our Lord God has done!

The tone of worship and blessings towards God in this prayer song of gratitude is as infectious as it is doctrinally rich.

The thoughts of the Lord towards us, that He even considered a wretch like me, the wonderful things He has for us cannot be numbered. There's not enough time or words in this life for us to declare all He has done for us.

All we can do is cry out, "Thank you!" And share this good news with others.

*Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.*

The blood of bulls and goats never took away sin. It may have cleansed the flesh to be in the presence of God in the temple made with hands, but to enter into His presence forever, in the Temple of Heaven, all He has ever required was faith in His promises.

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God*.

Have they not heard? The word of God has gone out to the world and not returned void. But those that harden their hearts, and stiffen their necks and refuse to obey the gospel of God.

As Jesus and the prophets taught:

**Matthew 13:13–16**
*Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.*

God has blessed us with the conviction of the Spirit, that even in the miry pit, we heard Him, and see with our eyes the mighty God, being converted and healed. Calling upon the name of the Lord.

**Romans 10:13**
*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

teachings.title: The man to whom the Lord imputeth not sin
teachings.summary: Repentance from dead works to faith in God saves by faith alone, and God promises not to impute sin to the believer but to remember it no more.
teachings.text:
**Hebrews 6:1**
*Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God*

Repentance from dead works and to faith towards God. Turning from means turning towards. From trusting in our works of righteousness to faith in God. This is the foundation that is built on the rock that is Christ.

And so, reckoned of faith, the man who does no works but believes, is saved by that faith alone. Paul quotes Davin from **Psalm 32**
*Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, Whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, And in whose spirit there is no guile*.

The Lord will not impute sin, our ledger is clean, our transgressions forgiven.

For what is sin?

**1 John 3:4**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.*

But we who believe not only are forgiven of sins past, but God will not impute sin to us. Our transgression is forgiven. This is a promise of God.

**Hebrews 10:17**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.*

teachings.title: Thou art all fair, my love
teachings.summary: The bride seen without blemish pictures believers made righteous and unblameable in Christ, and the sealed garden pictures eternal security.
teachings.text:
Chapter 4 opens with an ode to the beloved bride by her lover, the bridegroom. When he looks upon her he sees her fair beauty, her eyes as doves', her hair as the flocks of wild mountain goats. Picturing her black, flowing locks as the long, black, silky hair the goats have. When a herd of these dark goats grazes and moves down a steep mountain from a distance, the flowing movement creates a visual illusion of cascading hair.

He compares her teeth to the whitest of sheep, shorn and clean and notes there are none missing, a rarity to be sure in the ancient world.

Her lips, red as scarlet thread and her speech comely. Her temples and neck and breasts and scent, perfect and without blemish.

*Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.*

The poetic nature of the song, romanticizing the couples love, could be seen as hyperbole. The aura of beauty that comes with infatuation. The perfection we see when we are caught up in our love for the other.

But, as a spiritual allegory, we see the woman, who works the field and vineyard, black skinned, is without blemish when the King looks upon her. Just as we who are saved and sanctified by faith in Christ are pure when the Lord looks upon us. Clothed in righteousness. No sin imputed upon our new man.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

He has made us without blemish;

**Colossians 1:21–22**
*And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

Solomon's King sings passionately about his beloved; *How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse!* A sister of Israel, his spouse through their betrothal and marriage.

This is also how Jesus sees us, His beloved. We are His brothers and sisters, and spouse as a collective. Made one within the body of Christ.

**Matthew 12:50**
*For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother*.

His idealized view of us, despite our sin and despite our falling short of the glory of God, comes entirely by His love for us. That while we were sinners, Christ died for us. That He justifies the ungodly. That the Spirit quickens and seals us unto redemption.

So when Solomon compares his love to an inclosed garden, walled off, a spring shut up, barred from use by others. A fountain sealed, carrying the seal of the King, and so kept pure from pollution. In this allegory we see the promise of eternal security in Christ. We are eternally His.

The fruits of the garden are orchards, even pomegranates, and pleasant fruits, and flowers and spices used in ointments and perfume. Spikenard, the precious Himalayan plant, used to anoint Christ;

**Mark 14:3**
*And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.*

The odors of her garden are pleasing. Precious to the King.  Just as our fruit, our good works in Christ, are pleasing to Him.

*A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon*. He views us and the works we do for Him the same way, and we issue forth the living waters of the Spirit when we walk in His ways.

The chapter ends shifting to the beloved woman, the bride, calling upon her lord to enter her garden, *that the spices thereof may flow out.* Spiritually, calling upon the name of the Lord, that one may be saved, that God may eat His pleasant fruits.

teachings.title: Righteousness from the God of our salvation
teachings.summary: Believers are made clean by God's imputed righteousness received by faith, not by their own works, and Roman Catholicism's denial of imputation at the Council of Trent is a lie.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 24** is a meditation on the truth of the Christ, the Lord, King of Hosts. Creator of all things, and the truth of the way of righteousness for those that trust in Him.

The gospel message of the Psalms, sung in the Temple, performed by the chief musicians and the congregation is the inspired doctrines of God, and the focus is entirely Jesus.

They may have looked through a glass darkly, but the concepts of Christ are hammered home, in verse after verse, chorus and stanzas of praise for the name of God, the Holy One, the Lord.

Here in the 24th Psalm, David asks *Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place?*

Those with clean hands and pure hearts, who hasn't put their trust in vanity or lying lips, but who trusted the God of their salvation.

*He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.*

We are made clean of our sins, our hearts purified by the imputed righteousness of God. We receive these blessings by grace through faith, and access to the Kingdom, not by our own righteousness but by submitting to the righteousness that is God's.

**Romans 4:5–8**
*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

There are false religions that deny the imputation of righteousness by faith in Christ. They say that imputation is not taught in scripture. This is a lie.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Our righteousness is as a filthy rag, our works could never justify us before a holy and perfect God. But these men believing vanity, and swearing deceitfully, teach that man needs to establish their own righteousness through works of the law, and many are misled by this lie.

**Romans 10:2–4**
*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Roman Catholicsm rejects the idea that we are made righteous by receiving righteousness from the God of our salvation. The Council of Trent (Canon 11 on Justification) anathematized the idea that people are justified “by the sole imputation of the justice of Christ, or by the sole remission of sins” and that righteousness is "infused" by works, sacraments and "grace transforming a person," so that their own righteousness is established, rather than submitting to the righteousness of God.

But let God be true, and every man a liar. The generation of them that seek His face shall not be ashamed. All who come to the saving knowledge of Christ are made pure, in Him. Righteous, in Him.

**Titus 3:5–7**
*Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

The truth of imputed righteousness of God being given the believer is found throughout scripture. And thank God for His grace and mercy. That our sins are washed clean, justified by the blood, and remembered no more.

teachings.title: Blessed is the man whose sin is covered
teachings.summary: As David and Paul teach, God imputes righteousness without works and does not hold the believer's sins against him, and this good news must be received today before God's Spirit ceases to strive.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 32** opens with a very familiar and important doctrine, the understanding of God's forgiveness for sin in the saved believer's life. This foundational fact is repeated by Paul in the letter to the Romans;

**Romans 4:6–8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

The truth is that, in Christ, whether it was in David's day, or Paul's or our own, God forgives our past transgressions, covers our current sin, and will not hold our future sins and iniquity against us.

This positional standing of righteousness before God, despite our sins, through His imputed righteousness is made possible, through the Holy Spirit, by the renewal, the regeneration, the quickening of our spirit. The new man within us. Blessed is the man *in whose spirit there is no guile.*

We are given the Spirit of truth, that we may acknowledge our sin, knowing that we are forgiven of all sin, first, not by works but by faith.

The same good news today as in David's day. And this Psalm serves as an evangelical appeal.

David writes of a man who kept his silence, who hadn't called upon the name of the Lord, who suffered in their sins, bones waxing old and dried up by their roaring in the daytime, the heaviness of their iniquity weighing on them at night.

But the honesty and humility of acknowledging sin, not hiding anything from God (as if we could), confessing our transgressions unto the Lord, and being forgiven, is a blessing. Rioting in the daytime and being kept up at night by our conscience, being convicted in the Spirit, gives way to the peace that passes understanding, through the forgiveness that is given to us by God's mercy and grace.

David reminds us that there is a time where God may be sought, before it is too late.

**Isaiah 55:6**
*Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near*

God's Spirit will not always strive with man. There comes a time when those that put off or reject the truth, not acknowledging that they are sinners, lying to God and themselves, are no longer able to come to Him. Where He no longer extends His hand, because they have hardened their hearts and will not seek Him, even as they face destruction.

**Hebrews 4:7**
*Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.*

We have the example of those in the days of Noah, who mocked him for his faith in preparing the ark, and whose disobedient spirits who Christ preached to in Hell, were destroyed by the flood, never coming nigh unto God. Just as those left to God's wrath to come will not repent, despite the horrors of His judgment.

There is a time, it is today. There is a day, and it is the present. If you haven't accepted the truth that we are sinners in need of salvation, and that it is offered as a free gift to all who believe, through the grace of Almighty God, now is the time.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

teachings.title: Transgression, sin and iniquity forgiven
teachings.summary: Transgression is wilful rebellion, sin is missing the mark and iniquity is our twisted nature, and on the cross Christ bore all three, imputing His righteousness to believers so they are found not guilty, past, present and future.
teachings.text:
While it isn't entirely wrong to take the words transgression, sin and iniquity, and use them interchangeably, they do carry subtle differences in their meaning.

Transgression is the wilful rebellion against the truth of God and His commands. The transgression of Adam, for example, having one law to obey, and choosing of their own volition (even as Eve was deceived, Adam most assuredly knew better), deciding to be disobedient.

Sin, which the Bible says is the transgression of the Law, also carries with it the idea of missing the mark, falling short.

**Romans 3:23**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God*

We aren't able, in the flesh, to hit the mark, the target being the perfect holiness of God. Only Jesus Christ did.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Iniquity comes from the Hebrew word, *Avon*, meaning to twist, bend, or distort. The perverted and crooked nature of fallen man. The bent toward evil, the guilt that stays with us, and the perverted character that drives the outward actions. It is the *guile* or deceit mentioned in verse 2.

Our natural tendencies towards willful rebellion, to sin, and to lie to ourselves and others, including God, about the evil that we do. Excusing ourselves with lies.

Taken together, the blessed assurance that our transgressions, sins and iniquities are eternally forgiven demonstrates the mercy and grace of our Lord towards His children, through the suffering of Jesus.

**Isaiah 53:5–6**
*But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.*

He suffered these things for our iniquity and transgressions, that we may be purged. That His righteousness be imputed on our ledger, even as His blood blots away our sins.

Our transgressions are forgiven, our sin is covered, our iniquity will not be added to our account, because we are justified in Christ.

This accounting is a spiritual gift, applied to the ledger that in judgment, we are found not guilty by God.

(Some call this Penal Substitutionary Atonement, the idea that Jesus paid the price of the debt we owe, so that we do not have to receive the wages of sin. Many reject this idea. Whatever you want to call it, it is undeniable that Christ suffered that those who trust on Him, won't)

On the cross, Jesus carried away our rebellion, covered our failures with His blood, and cleared the ledger of our crooked nature by imputing His own perfect righteousness to us. Past, present and future. That we may be made the righteousness of God.

teachings.title: Trent's anathema on faith alone
teachings.summary: The Council of Trent's curse on justification by faith alone puts the Catholic Church against the Bible, which teaches salvation by grace through faith without works.
teachings.text:
The Council of Trent, on salvation by faith alone:

CANON IX.-If any one saith, that by faith alone the impious is justified; in such wise as to mean, that nothing else is required to co-operate in order to the obtaining the grace of Justification, and that it is not in any way necessary, that he be prepared and disposed by the movement of his own will; let him be anathema

CANON XII.-If any one saith, that justifying faith is nothing else but confidence in the divine mercy which remits sins for Christ’s sake; or, that this confidence alone is that whereby we are justified; let him be anathema.

The Bible is anathema to the Catholic Church. Jesus Christ Himself, and Paul, Peter, James, all heretics and anathema to them.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**Romans 11:6**
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

**Romans 3:20**
*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
 *For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.*

**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

teachings.title: Enoch walked with God
teachings.summary: Enoch, translated by faith and prophet of Christ's coming, is the example of walking separated and pleasing God, and the patriarchs picture the steps of coming to Christ.
teachings.text:
**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.

teachings.title: Too late, reprobate
teachings.summary: Reprobation is real and comes after God has repeatedly led a man to repentance and been rebuffed, so readers must accept the free gift of salvation now because the Spirit will not pursue them forever.
teachings.text:
I sincerely pray that everyone who comes to the channel today takes the time to read the scriptures I posted here, and study them out for themselves. Comparing scripture with scripture. Proving all things.

In two different epistles, one to Gentiles and the other to Israelites, God inspires Paul in the Spirit to lay out His doctrines that we may know and understand Him. It isn't gnostic revelation, but God reasoning with man that we may be able to go on to perfection, throughly furnished unto all good works. Telling us directly that we may know His will. And in both books, after establishment of the primary doctrines of Christ, we are given the explanation of the reprobate doctrine.

It is also one of the primary doctrines taught in Peter's letters, and Jude. It is the subject of many of Christ's sermons, especially Matthew 23. It is talked about in the OT, and shown us in Exodus as Pharoah goes through the process of hardening his heart until God hardens it forever.

Reprobation is real and it happens after God has repeatedly led one to repentance, only to be rebuffed. There is a point where it is too late, even if that point is death.

If you do not know for sure, today, right now, that you are saved. That you have eternal life. That you have been adopted by God into the promise of His kingdom, please consider His word. Don't wait. Now is the time. Accept that free gift. Repent from your dead works and vain traditions and accept the free gift of salvation paid for by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

Because the Spirit will not pursue you forever. It can become too late. And reprobates live a hell on earth of misery and filthy affections, until going finally to the Hell that awaits them, to be burned forever. Too late, reprobate.

Don't let this become you.

teachings.title: Predestinated in Christ, not chosen to believe
teachings.summary: Predestination in Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 is in Christ, not God choosing who will believe, since God will have all men to be saved and draws all men, so Calvinism and limited atonement are doctrines of devils rooted in pride.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-6**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved*.

So what is this that is predestined? The saved? Or Christ Jesus by whom we are saved?

Calvinists read this and **Romans 8**, and place the emphasis on themselves, rather than Christ, and so, they claim, that God picks who will believe. This doctrine of devils, like all false gospels, is based on putting themselves before the Lord. Just as works salvation is predicated on the person's own righteousness, not Christ's, the special boy doctrine makes it that they are the elect, not of Jesus perfect work, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that all who believe on Him will be saved, but by God's "sovereign will."

But we know that God's will is not for a chosen few.

**1 Timothy 2:3-4**
*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.*

If God exerted His sovereign will, we would all be saved.

As Jesus says,

*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

Every one.

Limited atonement is a doctrine of devils. It is based on pride.

So we know that all who believe are predestinated in Christ that they will have eternal life, sealed by the Spirit, and if they walk in tha Spirit, will be conformed to the use of God, that we may become separated, to be servants of the Gospel.

And so continuing the theme of Romans 8, the context of which is the works of the Spirit.

That while we are yet in the flesh, knowing the day of redemption will free us from that wretched state, that the Spirit helps heal our infirmities that led us to sin and conforms us to His will, so long as we walk after the Spirit, not feeding the flesh with the things of this world. That the Spirit within us acts also as an intercessor to bring our needs before the Father, so that His will be done in us.

And so, the good news;

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

Who is called? Who is drawn to faith in God's promise?

**John 12:32-33**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. This he said, signifying what death he should die.*

All men. But few will answer this call, and seek to be transformed to fulfill His intended purpose for us. The harvest is great but the laborers few. Strait is the gate and narrow the way and few there be that find it. Every name of every person born of water upon this earth is in the book of life. But their names are stricken from it when they die in sin, unbelieving. (Or reprobates, twice-dead)

No where in the Bible do we see names added, only erased. God's foreknowledge, knowing of the end from the beginning, means He knows who will answer the call. It doesn't mean He selects them.

teachings.title: A trail of blood of believers
teachings.summary: Saved believers stand in an unbroken line of faith, bearing fruit after its kind from Abel through the apostles to today, linked by a trail of martyrs' blood persecuted by Rome and the false church.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 1:11**
*And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.*

**Matthew 21:43**
*Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.*

Matthew 7:16-18
*Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.*

**Philippians 1**:**4-11**
*Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace. For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ. And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment; That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ. Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.*

**Romans 1:16-17**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.*

I am a saved Christian. Born again by the faith that was shared to me by another saved Christian, who in turn believed and was converted by yet another saved. Christian. A line of succession going back to the beginning of the world. That the just live by faith and bear fruit after its own kind.

A line of believers stretching back to Adam. To Abel. To Seth and Enos.

The same faith of Abraham who believed the Lord and it was counted upon him for righteousness. The same faith that makes up the record of the "Hall of faith," in Hebrews chapter 11.

The same faith preached by John, the Baptist in the wilderness, taught by Christ Himself during His earthly ministry, given to the apostles as the keys to overcome death and hell. Preached on the day of Pentecost. Given to the Jews and to the Greek. The salvation that is by calling upon the name of the Lord. By believing on the finished work of Christ Jesus as the propitiation of our sin.

And, like the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah, and of Jesus and the Apostles, and of the believers persecuted by the Jews and the Romans, a trail of blood that links believing Christians today to those that were martyred for the same faith in the same Gospel of grace and reconciliation. A trail of blood that continued through the persecution by Constantine's cult, through the dark ages, during the Reformation, under Bloody Mary, and that will mark the great tribulation to come.

teachings.title: Why the law cannot save
teachings.summary: Keeping God's law is for our good but not for salvation, since no one can keep it all; the law is a schoolmaster bringing us to Christ to be justified freely by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
We should also remember that obedience to the civil laws of God are for our benefit. For our good always. That it be well with us. That it prolongs our days and that we are preserved alive. Not for salvation. Not for our own righteousness.

The law is a schoolmaster, teaching us our need for salvation in Christ.

**Galatians 3:24-27**
*Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.*

Because;

I*t shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.*

If we observed to do **all** these commandments, it would be our righteousness. We would have to glory.

**Romans 4:1-12**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.*

But knowing that it is impossible in our flesh to observe all these things, we understand that it is God's glory that His mercy is revealed.

**James 2:10**
*For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.*

**Romans 3:10-12**
*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God.*
*They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.*

As Paul writes a few verses later, *There is no fear of God before their eyes.* But as Moses writes here in **Deuteronomy 6**, under the same Spirit as Paul, we are to learn the law of God and keep it in our hearts, in our minds, *That thou mightest fear the Lord thy God*.

And in that fear, that respect and love of the Lord, we may know we have His mercy towards us:

**Romans 3:23-26**
*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.*

teachings.title: The root of the righteous shall not be moved
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries a consistent gospel message: a man is made good by faith that comes by the word, and the root of righteousness is Christ, not Israel as dispensationalists claim nor Peter as Catholics claim.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 12** opens with another reminder that loving instruction and knowledge is precious, and the way of righteousness, while hating correction and wisdom is brutish and wicked.

And verse two reiterates that a good man - the just, wise, fearful of God who seeks after knowledge and walks in His ways, obtains favor from the Lord, but the wicked are condemned.

**Proverbs 9:10**
*The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding*.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

**Romans 5:1-2**
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God*...

We see how a man is made good, by the fear of God and hearing of His word, by faith seeking Him and truth, and by faith we have access to His grace, we obtain the favor of the Lord, receiving His gift of salvation.

The consistent gospel message of Proverbs cannot be overlooked.

Wickedness cannot establish a man, but the root of Righteousness, that is Christ Jesus, shall not be moved. He is the "root of Jesse" and a "branch of righteousness" (**Isaiah 11, Jeremiah 23:5-6**), established as the foundational righteousness for all believers. Through faith, believers are grafted into this root, allowing them to bear the fruit of righteousness, by the precious seed of His word.

Romans 11:16-18 
*For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

Dispensationalists will claim the root is Israel, but it has always been Christ. Just as Catholics will claim Peter, "a stone," is the rock, which actually is the profession that Jesus is Christ. Because no other foundation can be laid;

**1 Corinthians 3:11**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

All wisdom leads to Christ.

**Matthew 7:24-25** 
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

teachings.title: Delight in the saints, not Lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Calling Jesus Lord is a saved believer's statement of fact, not the false gospel of Lordship salvation; our good works add nothing to God but are poured out in love and service to the saints.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 16** presents another sacred hymn celebrating the Lord's salvation, the eternal security of the believer, and the promise of the risen Christ.

The preservation of the saints is the hope of all who place their trust in God. Our very being cries out to Him for salvation, recognizing He is Lord.

Note here that this isn't "Lordship salvation," a false gospel that says you must "make Jesus the Lord of your life" to be saved. It is saved believers, already trusting Him to save us, recognizing that He IS the Lord, as a statement of fact.

David writes, *Thou art my Lord: my goodness extendeth not to thee; But to the saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent, in whom is all my delight.* The good that we do isn't for Him, it adds nothing to the holy and perfect God.

The idea that Jesus needs us to make Him Lord, that by our "turning from sin," we justify ourselves before God, is hubris. It's a false gospel.

The good we do comes from Him, and is poured out to the brothers and sisters, the saints. We benefit others, and they glorify God. We obey His judgements, to one another's profit.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

We submit ourselves to the righteousness of God. We do not seek to establish our own righteousness, but to magnify His.

**Romans 10:3–4**
*For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

David's burden is for the saints in the earth, his delight is to the excellent of God. Just as we are commanded to.

**John 13:34–35**
*A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.*

While we should seek to live peaceably with all men, we should especially look with love upon our fellow believers.

**Galatians 6:9–10**
*And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.*

This is the message that we have heard from the beginning. It is our job as Christians. It is how we are to know one another. Not keeping to ourselves or seeking out own profit. Certainly not by hating our brothers.

1 John 3:10–11
*In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.*

This is the mind of Christ, to be servants, one to another. To delight in others.

The ultimate expression of humility isn't thinking less of yourself, but not thinking of yourself at all. And the humbleness of submission to God's righteousness should naturally turn to our service for others. Not to add to God's goodness our filthy rags, but to glorify His goodness in us.

teachings.title: The vanity of riches before death
teachings.summary: Wise and fool, rich and poor all die, riches cannot ransom a soul, and only the fear of the Lord and redemption through Christ give hope in the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
Psalm 49 is a meditation on the futility of life, in the building of of riches, honor and name, when death awaits everyone, rich or poor, wise or fool.

This reflection on life's vanities ties to Solomon's writings in **Ecclesiastes**, from the call to harken to the preacher to the vanity of life and the only remedy, fearing the Lord and receiving His blessing.

**Ecclesiastes 2:16**
*For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.*

This echoes the same sentiment found in verse 10;

*For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.*

**Ecclesiastes 5:15**
*As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.*

Solomon learned at the feet of his father, and after careful study of all the things his wealth and power availed him of, with the wisdom above other men, granted by God's grace, he would come to the same conclusions David sang of.

The call to incline your ear to hear wisdom, to listen to the dark sayings and parables. To seek understanding is a major theme of Solomon's **Proverbs**;

**Proverbs 4:7**
*Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.*

David teaches us the same lessons in Psalms. The wisdom of God is most valuable, because in that knowledge we may find eternal life.

David expresses confidence in his salvation. He is not afraid when the time comes to be given the wages of his sin, the iniquity of his heels, the death that awaits us all, the consequences of our own making.

Why should we fear in the days of evil, that comes our own making? He knows his redemption is a gift of God. But the man trusting his riches has no hope at all in that day. They cannot redeem themselves or their brothers, and cannot pay the ransom due God for their sins.

Again, this idea that man's riches are worthless in the judgment, that they do nothing for the dead, is repeated by Solomon;

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

**Proverbs 27:24**
*For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?*

Their way is folly. The wise man dies like the fool, like the brute, and all their wealth is left for others. But the precious redemption of the soul, that one lives forever and shall not see corruption, that is of God, through faith in the Lord Christ Jesus.

**1 Timothy 2:5–6**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

David laments the fact that worldly prosperity deceives the wealthy, their own riches fooling them into a false sense of security. This is the larger context of the preaching of Christ;

**Matthew 19:23–26**
*Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.*

The only hope of man, rich or poor, is God. Only in Him is salvation possible.

**Proverbs 15:16**
*Better is little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith.*

The blessings of this life are not a hope for the next. The praise of men is vanity before the Throne of an almighty and holy God.

Agur's  prayer in **Proverbs** directly addresses this wisdom;

**Proverbs 30:8-9**
*Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*
